questions.context: The narrator belongs to the Heralds, an order the texts invent: their Medical University, their Monastery, 'the Savant' at their Archivum in Urbis. Canon: Guild Accord, Division of Alchemetrica (alchemy), Archmagus-ranked (its senior grade), 'Youngest Recorded S-Grade in Accord History', bound to the Dawn Guard's teaching vow; and in the road years, 'Four separate Accord assessments called Mu-jin temperamentally unsuited to field deployment. He went wherever he was sent.' Vol I's Monastery sends him to the king as 'the least expensive to lose'.

options.label: The Accord grades and posts him in every volume
options.consequence: The errand to the king becomes an Accord posting, and the four assessments arrive as he lives them. Archmagus appears only once he holds it, and only in others' mouths, such as Gillus's address. The Herald schools stay as places he studies.

options.label: The Accord appears only from Vol III, after the rank
options.consequence: Vols I–II show him outside any institution; Vol III's letter and title page carry the Division and the vow. Simpler, but it hides the assessments that sent him everywhere.

options.label: The Accord replaces the Herald institutions outright
options.consequence: University, Monastery and Archivum become Accord bodies. Removes an invented order but rewrites much of Vol I's setting and collides with the setting questions about the Heralds.

questions.rec_reason: Canon has the Guild Accord forming now, and Mu-jin drafted its alliance terms himself; his Arena speech speaks of 'the period before the Accord existed'. It enters the Codex once he holds the rank.
questions.evidence: Mu-jin card:13, :27, :85, :176; R52-21; vol1_vault:72; Vol II docx:183; Codex page:13

questions.title: His part in Category Three and failing seals
questions.question: What is Mu-jin's relationship to Category Three work (completing a dead person's unfinished decision into a body) and to the seals that fail on it?
questions.context: The Necrocursica says the Third Corruption begins when the final Mortalis Sealing Glyph (the glyph that closes a working) is botched. Mu-jin's card: Fixation Anchor Sense 'feels a Draft's Sealing Glyphs the way most people feel a held breath', knowing streets away when one fails; Anamnesis matured; no Mortalis harmonization (attunement to the death Wellspring). Canon: authorizing a process needs 'genuine Wellspring harmonization' with it. Sight Through the Glass, his lens-off read, costs a migraine and about 2% of his reserve.

options.label: Detector only: he feels seals fail, never performs Category Three
options.consequence: He is the Codex's witness of failing seals: the passive sense is free and reaches streets away, a full lens-off read costs its migraine. He diagnoses and warns but cannot perform; Genesio completes through his Anamnesis, never his authority.

options.label: Give him Mortalis harmonization
options.consequence: He can perform Category Three himself, opening larger plots. His card gains a fifth harmonization with a reason in his Temperance history, and the Necrocursica's picture of him as an outside witness goes.

options.label: Keep his senses out of the Mortalis material
options.consequence: No risk to the card; the Codex never uses his seal sense. It wastes the strongest link between the author and his subject and leaves him oddly blind to what he writes about.

questions.rec_reason: It uses his traits as they stand, respects the harmonization rule, and gives the Codex a fair limit: a sense with a range and a cost, and an operation he cannot author.
questions.evidence: Mu-jin card:48, :82, :96, :98; Spirit Rune Arts:36, :50; Necrocursica:173, :465; Vol III docx:228; Summon Register:34

questions.title: Whether and how Rimward enters the Codex
questions.question: Does the Codex touch Rimward, where Mu-jin asked with no Draft and 'something answered', and if so, how much does it say?
questions.context: At Rimward a wall fell toward a boy; with no Draft (a drawn working circle) fast enough, 'He asked without one, as though he held a standing he did not have… Something answered.' He lost his right eye. He told Ara he could not give it 'a shape' and would say it to her first when he could. The Correction, 'Correspondence is not reflection. It is response', is a shape; his summoning is already 'a trained correspondence with the Continuum's own archived intention'. Canon never says what answered.

options.label: Never named; the Correction carries it by implication
options.consequence: Honours 'he would not discuss what had answered'. A reader who knows Rimward hears it under Vol III; nothing new enters canon, and the promise to Ara stays unkept on the page.

options.label: Named as his question; what answered stays unnamed
options.consequence: Vol III opens on Rimward as the question the Trace answers: he writes the wall, the eye and the law of response, never who responded. Keeps the promise to Ara and his refusal to invent a shape.

options.label: Named with a mechanism: an over-warrant took the eye
options.consequence: He writes that he claimed a standing he lacked and the Seal deducted his eye (an over-warrant, canon's charge for overclaiming). The Counted Speech's deduction list gains 'the eyes', and his house law 'gets nothing' needs a note.

questions.rec_reason: It turns his canon promise into Vol III's reason to exist while keeping the card's refusal: he writes what he can now shape, the response, and still not who responded.
questions.evidence: Mu-jin card:163, :178; Vaeloris:1872-1880; Ara card:177; Codex page:71-77; Open Crucible:20, :23; Counted Speech:110, :149

questions.title: His credit in the residue theory
questions.question: The Necrocursica credits the four residue categories to 'De Raits, Thom, and Trismegistus'; what credit does Mu-jin keep?
questions.context: Residue categories are the kinds of trace the dead leave behind; the fourth, the Volitional Trace, is what Category Three completion runs on. The Necrocursica credits all four to the three men jointly, yet its Appendix II calls the Codex's author an outsider who met the work 'through its outputs', and its cross-reference lists him as annotator of the Thom Submission. The Codex page says his Vol III testimony entered it into canon. At the Arena he condemns a culprit who 'studied the same source material'.

options.label: Co-formalizer with Gillus and Thom, as the Necrocursica says
options.consequence: Mu-jin helped build the theory the villains use and later condemns its use at the Arena: heavier guilt, a sharper Arena scene. Appendix II's 'from the outside' and the annotator credit are recut to match.

options.label: Cut him: De Raits and Thom only
options.consequence: The Necrocursica's credit drops him and he stays the pure outside witness. Clean, but Vol III's testimony entering the canon loses its point, and the Codex page's credit line changes.

options.label: Witness and namer: he named it, Gillus and Thom built it
options.consequence: The Necrocursica credits the method to De Raits and Thom and the name to Mu-jin's testimony; he annotates the Thom Submission. Matches its own cross-reference, Appendix II and the Codex page.

questions.rec_reason: Three of the texts' own statements already describe him this way. The Arena speech stays honest, and he still carries a real share: the testimony that turned a theory into Accord canon.
questions.evidence: Necrocursica:93, :465, :477, :497; Codex page:61-63, :85; Vol II docx:261; Arena scene:25

sections.title: Malphas and the Necrocursica
sections.intro: The Necrocursica becomes Malphas's treatise. These questions place it in his life, before or after the Becoming, and decide how much of the lich shows in the writer.

questions.title: When in his life he writes it
questions.question: At what point in Malphas's life does he write the Necrocursica's core text: before Invocation, at it, after Greyshaft Nine, or as a lich?
questions.context: The preface: two visitors compel him at Genesio, his left hand is 'not yet fully healed', and he writes fourteen months, first under protest, then past the brief. His card: expelled, solitary, then Invocation (Stage IX, when greater powers become co-authors; he 'stopped working alone'), recorded as relief, then worse within a year or two; then the Greyshaft Nine cell of The Mother; then the Becoming (Stage XIV, his death into a lich). The Night's Watch scene shows him alive at Greyshaft Nine.

options.label: At Invocation: the compulsion is when he stopped working alone
options.consequence: The preface stays close to as written. The months past the brief are Invocation's relief; the 'worse' a year or two later is The Mother. The warnings read as sincere and tragic, written in the Codex I years.

options.label: In the solitary years before Invocation
options.consequence: Keeps 'You have not retired. You are avoiding', but the compulsion is no longer his turning point, and co-writing clashes with the card's 'let no hand but his own near the bench'.

options.label: In the nine years after Greyshaft Nine, before Aetherion
options.consequence: Every warning comes after Project Zombification, so the candour reads as cover. The Codex, set in Mu-jin's youth, could not read it, and the planned book's nine-year gap must hold fourteen months at Genesio.

options.label: After the Becoming, as a lich
options.consequence: The healing-hand line goes, since a lich's hand does not heal; nobody compels a Level 475 Archmaster; the author refutes his own thesis that the dead do not think. A full rewrite.

questions.rec_reason: It matches Invocation's recorded shape, relief then worse, without breaking the card's solitary years, and keeps a living, sincere author ahead of the Codex and Greyshaft Nine. The fit is thematic: his compellers are people, not powers.
questions.evidence: Malphas card 20-24, 125-136; Temperance Stages, Stage IX; Necrocursica 5, 21, 37-53; Night's Watch 183; book bible 32, 86

questions.title: Is he the Heresiology's Compelled Author?
questions.question: Is Malphas the Heresiology's 'Compelled Author' (Case II), and so its example of Submission before his canon corruption, Fermentation Perverted?
questions.context: The Heresiology (canon's treatise on seven ways alchemy goes wrong) describes the Necrocursica's author in Case II: 'pulled by access and manipulated through need', his warning kept in a footnote. Submission is talent dissolving 'into another will', like the scholar working 'in exchange for archive access'; Codex II uses the author as its example. Malphas's card files him under Fermentation Perverted (valuing rot for its yield), yet Dissolution is his primary Wellspring, and The Mother, his cult, wants 'a sealed text'. Your answer also fixes which corruption Mu-jin names in the author in Volume II.

options.label: Yes: Submission first, then Fermentation Perverted
options.consequence: Case II and Codex II's example stand with the name changed. The preface adds the bargain, sealed Genesio stacks for his pen, beside the coercion. His card's Lore gains a first corruption: the perverted form of his own primary Wellspring.

options.label: Yes, but read as Distillation Perverted (Sanitized Truth)
options.consequence: Case II's footnote matches Distillation's 'manuals whose warnings survive only as footnotes'. Codex II needs another Submission example, and his card gains Distillation, turning horror into clean procedure, as his first slide.

options.label: No: pure coercion, with no bargain
options.consequence: The preface stands as written. Case II's 'pulled by access' is reworded, which is a canon edit, and Codex II's Submission chapter loses its example.

options.label: No: he wanted the stacks, and Case II misreads him
options.consequence: In-world scholars thought him coerced; he went for the sealed stacks (his canon want: to obtain the unattainable). Works only if the Heresiology is one school's reading, and readers must distrust a doctrinal text.

questions.rec_reason: Case II's wording already fits access plus need; Submission perverts Dissolution, his primary; his Invocation, handing responsibility to something that signed nothing, is Submission-shaped; and one life then shows two canon corruptions in order.
questions.evidence: Heresiology 70-76, 111-127, 209; Codex II docx 85, 111, 165; Malphas card 21-23, 45, 53; The Mother 31; R60-25

questions.title: Who the titled second compeller is
questions.question: The preface names Gillus De Raits and a second visitor who 'goes by a title'; who is that second visitor, and what marked his hand?
questions.context: Gillus exists only in the Codex and Papers (Stage VII, Mortalis primary). The persuasion 'left an impression on his left hand'. Canon candidates: a Sancta Lux Inquisitor (a Church officer who may sentence in the field; unlicensed high working is punished by branding); the Pyraeon Forge Academy, which expelled Malphas and 'later lost a strategist to him', Zeraphine Drowl; or the power that answered at his Invocation. The Seventh-Corruption man at a Genesio waystation may be Gillus, though the author never approached him.

options.label: Gillus plus a title never revealed
options.consequence: The Codex and Papers links stay and the blank is deliberate. Least new canon, but the hand wound has no findable cause.

options.label: Gillus plus Zeraphine Drowl, then the Academy's tactician
options.consequence: The Academy gets its first face, her canon betrayal starts at his confinement, and the hand mark is hers. Her card's Lore gains the meeting, fixing her as an Academy officer at the date ML1 sets.

options.label: Gillus plus a Sancta Lux Inquisitor; the mark is a brand
options.consequence: Ties to the Gate's penalties (R60-16, R60-17) and roots his wish to break the Gate. Adds Sancta Lux to his past, and an Inquisitor commissioning necromancy needs a motive.

options.label: Gillus plus the power that answered at Invocation, wearing a title
options.consequence: The preface becomes the first sighting of what took him at the Becoming ('had been waiting'). No new faction; the 'impression' is its mark, which his bones must still carry.

questions.rec_reason: Two canon pages already say the Academy later lost a strategist to him; this makes the meeting where it began, gives the Academy the face its lore asks for, and leaves the hand a findable wound.
questions.evidence: Necrocursica 5, 37, 365-373; Zeraphine card 17, 25-28; The Mother, Relations; Gate page 61, 76; Malphas card 20-24; Codex III docx 50

questions.title: The name on the title page
questions.question: What name does Malphas sign the Necrocursica with, and the poetry the Codex says he published?
questions.context: The text signs 'N. Ren, Genesio', and the Codex and Papers cite 'Noxinus Ren' dozens of times. Malphas treats names as evidence: a name is 'the only thing... the Accord can actually prosecute', so he wants any file 'built off a word I chose'. The Heresiology describes him 'without naming him'. The planned Night Watch book (not yet canon) gives him a later alias, Doctor Osric Salter.

options.label: His own name, Malphas
options.consequence: The sealed text becomes a file with his real name on it, which his naming method forbids. The Heresiology's 'without naming him' weakens, and every Codex and Papers citation changes.

options.label: 'Noxinus Ren', a pen name he chose
options.consequence: No separate Noxinus exists; the name is his mask. Codex and Papers citations need few edits, the alias matches his naming discipline and the later Salter alias, and his card gains a 'written as' line.

options.label: Unsigned, or a descriptive signature
options.consequence: His identity stays hidden, but the Codex friendship, Appendix II and the marginal notes lose the name they hang on, and dozens of citations need a descriptor.

questions.rec_reason: Most in character: the file gets built off a word he picked. It honours the replacement, since Noxinus is no longer a separate man, and spares the most text.
questions.evidence: Necrocursica 5, 21, 69, 489; Night's Watch 223, 227; The Mother 51; Malphas card 45, 135; Codex II docx 211

questions.title: The office on his title page
questions.question: The title page calls him 'Alchemist-Scribe of the Trans-Alftian Accord'; what standing, if any, should the converted title page give him?
questions.context: His card: expelled from the Pyraeon Forge Academy, 'Unbound in life', and afterwards he 'answered to no school and no house'. Canon has no Alchemist-Scribe post and no Trans-Alftian Accord, only one Guild Accord, still forming (the regional name is cut as a fix). His preface calls him 'alchemist, sometime astronomer, unwilling expert', which suits his epithet, Ferment of Stars.

options.label: No office: 'alchemist, sometime astronomer' only
options.consequence: The title page uses his own preface words and keeps the Academy hidden behind the pen name. Card untouched; the page loses its joke.

options.label: A sentence title his compellers imposed, which he mocks
options.consequence: Something like 'Scribe to the Genesio Archivum, by order'. Keeps the page's rhythm, shows Submission on its face, and stays card-safe: a leash is not a house he answers to.

options.label: His canon standing, stated openly
options.consequence: 'Expelled from the Pyraeon Forge Academy, declared a metaphysical threat': darkly funny, but it ties the alias to Malphas on the page, so it only works if he signs as Malphas.

questions.rec_reason: It keeps the confinement's logic and the page's shape, makes Submission visible, and needs no card change: a title handed to a prisoner is not a school he answers to.
questions.evidence: Malphas card 19-20, 125-128; Necrocursica 5, 37; Guild Accord in the Modern Era, section II; R60-09, R60-18

questions.title: How Malphas and Mu-jin know each other
questions.question: How do Malphas and Kwon Mu-jin know each other, now that they wrote the paired books?
questions.context: The Codex's Noxinus is Mu-jin's older friend: he lodges with him, sets an alchemical primer on his kitchen table, and brings the manuscript ('Tell me what I wrote'). Appendix II answers Mu-jin's third volume: 'File them adjacent.' Canon: Mu-jin learned alchemy at court under Doryun; primers are controlled texts issued only on registration; The Mother 'recruits by offering what the state has refused'. In the Arena scene Mu-jin describes Malphas's method without knowing the man.

options.label: Old friends, and Mu-jin knows or learns he is Malphas
options.consequence: The Codex stays warm and the Arena speech becomes knowing: Mu-jin keeps a secret about The Mother's founder. Both cards gain the tie, and the planned book must settle whether he recognises Salter.

options.label: Friends under the pen name; Mu-jin never learns it is Malphas
options.consequence: Codex scenes keep the name. The primer becomes a later unlicensed text passed outside the Gate (the state's lock on who may learn magic), not his first alchemy. The planned book must keep Salter's face from Mu-jin.

options.label: Noxinus stays a separate friend who carries Malphas's text
options.consequence: The friendship survives without Malphas; Noxinus becomes a go-between and stays a character. The Codex's 'Noxinus's treatise' lines and the pen-name choice change.

options.label: No personal tie: Mu-jin knows only the text
options.consequence: The shared lodgings, the primer and the 'Tell me what I wrote' night go to Paracelsus or are cut. The Arena irony and book plan stay; Codex II loses its most human scene.

questions.rec_reason: It keeps the Codex's affection and Appendix II, respects Mu-jin's court training, turns the primer into Malphas already breaking the Gate, and sharpens the Arena irony.
questions.evidence: Volume the First 24, 87; Codex II docx 91; Kwon Mu-jin card 164; Gate page 57; The Mother 22; Arena scene 17, 64; book bible 153

questions.title: One Necrocursica or two editions
questions.question: The extant text cites all three Codex volumes, yet the Codex reads it first; did Malphas write one Necrocursica or two editions?
questions.context: Codex I has it already written while Mu-jin is at Castlefall ('I have not read it'); Codex II reads a manuscript with three residue categories (kinds of trace the dead leave behind) and the footnote 'Never claim it is the soul'. The extant text has four categories 'now formalized' with the Codex author's help, cites the Codex and the Papers, and Appendix II answers Volume III. The Papers' two 'twelve years' put it about 24 years back, a third clock.

options.label: Two editions: an early manuscript, then a sealed edition
options.consequence: Codex I and II read the first (three categories, the footnote), written in the Codex I years. The extant text is the later sealed edition, with a short edition note. The Papers' 'twelve years' (lines 75, 101) are re-dated to K1's timeline.

options.label: One text, written after Volume III
options.consequence: Codex I's 'I have not read it' and Codex II's reading scene and footnote exchange go. The Heresiology's Case II loses its source scene.

options.label: One text, written before the Codex events
options.consequence: Strip the Codex and Papers citations, the 'formalized' credit and Appendix II. Loses 'File them adjacent', and four categories then contradict Codex II's three.

questions.rec_reason: Fewest edits, every event in all five texts survives, and the young Malphas and the older one each get a layer. One date fix in the Papers closes the third clock.
questions.evidence: Codex I extract 44, 88; Codex II docx 89-103; Necrocursica 25, 93, 109, 173, 477; Papers 75, 101; Heresiology 209

questions.title: The warning footnote and whose hand
questions.question: Canon says the compelled author's warning 'survived as a footnote'; who writes that footnote, and does it survive into the sealed edition?
questions.context: Heresiology Case II: 'The warning survived as a footnote'; Sanitized Truth (Distillation Perverted) cites 'necromantic manuals whose warnings survive only as footnotes'. In Codex II the author says 'I wrote it with the warning in it', and Mu-jin quotes the footnote ('Never claim it is the soul') as what separates the text from its most dangerous form. The extant Necrocursica has no footnote, only archive stamps, but its Archivum copy carries a marginal note in the Codex author's hand.

options.label: Malphas writes it, and both editions carry it
options.consequence: Restore the footnote to the extant text. Case II stands exactly; a man canon files under Fermentation shows conscience twice.

options.label: He writes it; the sealed edition drops it; Mu-jin restores it
options.consequence: The first edition has it, as Codex II quotes. The sealed edition cuts it, and Mu-jin's note in the Archivum copy carries it back. 'Survived' becomes literal, and the cut shows his descent on the page.

options.label: A later hand adds it: an archivist or the Papers author
options.consequence: Malphas never wrote a warning. Case II changes from 'the author kept a conscience' to 'someone else did', and Codex II's 'I wrote it with the warning in it' and footnote exchange are rewritten.

options.label: No footnote anywhere
options.consequence: Case II, Sanitized Truth's example and Codex II's footnote passage are all rewritten.

questions.rec_reason: Every canon line holds, the Archivum copy's existing Mu-jin annotation carries it, and the gap between editions shows Malphas losing his conscience in his own text.
questions.evidence: Heresiology 127, 209; Codex overview page 43; Volume the Second 137; Codex II docx 103, 111; Necrocursica 13, 25, 449

questions.title: How openly the margins foreshadow his fall
questions.question: How openly should the Necrocursica foreshadow the man Malphas becomes?
questions.context: The text already walks into his future. The Fifth Corruption (preferring the dead) ends 'treat this document as a confession'; the Sixth is naming; the Third (an unsealed made-body grows 'more itself') echoes the Ferriby wedge growing in a sealed tin; 'bleed' is later The Mother's cover word; Category Three is Thom's scaled work. The title page promises annotation 'with growing enthusiasm by the same'.

options.label: Leave the ironies unspoken
options.consequence: Minimal edits; core and margins stay as written, and readers who know The Mother find the echoes themselves. 'Bleed' stays an unmarked private joke.

options.label: Sealed-edition margins show his drift
options.consequence: Short notes by the older, living Malphas against the Third, Fifth and Sixth Corruptions and Category Three, each a step over his own line. The core warnings stay sincere; the document reads in two voices.

options.label: A lich's margin layer after the Becoming
options.consequence: The dead author corrects himself in his own hand, but the extant copy then postdates Greyshaft Nine, the archive's present, and every present-day citation of it must move later.

questions.rec_reason: It uses the margins the title page already promises, keeps the Stage IX warnings sincere, and lets readers watch him cross his lines without a future-dated layer.

questions.title: Whether The Mother uses the Necrocursica
questions.question: Does The Mother, Malphas's cult, use the Necrocursica, and if so how?
questions.context: The Mother recruits 'by offering what the state has refused', wants 'a sealed text', and teaches what the Gate (the state's lock on who may learn magic) forbids. A live rule makes it 'a religious following of the Becoming', though its Greyshaft Nine culture works while he is alive. In the Arena scene Mu-jin says the culprit studied 'the same source material I have studied'.

options.label: Not at all
options.consequence: The book stays in the sealed stacks and the cult never cites it. The echoes stay literary, and no page changes.

options.label: A working text he teaches from memory
options.consequence: Each culture's methods trace to its protocols, so anyone who has read it can recognise the cult's work: a counter someone can find. The Mother's page gains one line; the Arena speech becomes that recognition.

options.label: The sealed text the cult is trying to recover
options.consequence: The founder lost his own book to the Archivum, and the cult's 'sealed text' aim becomes his manuscript. A ready thread for a Front (a tracked threat clock); The Mother's page names it.

options.label: Scripture of the Becoming
options.consequence: Ties it to the live cult rule, but the living Greyshaft culture predates the Becoming, so the scripture reading needs a later date than the cult's first cells.

questions.rec_reason: It fits the cult's Gate-breaking aim, gives a findable counter (read the book, recognise the work), and matches the Arena line without editing the scene.
questions.evidence: The Mother 22, 31-33; R60-24; R60-25; Arena scene 64; Night's Watch 215, 223

questions.title: Full resurrection: impossible or only forbidden
questions.question: The Necrocursica calls full resurrection 'Category Four... not authorized'; should the converted text call it forbidden, or impossible?
questions.context: Canon's page on how the dead cross over (The Crossing) says necromancy 'does not raise the dead, which is not a thing that can be done'; a live rule makes death 'almost always permanent', excepting liches and the undead. The Heresiology treats resurrection claims as a heresy marker. The text's Category IV implies possible but banned, and its author later becomes the setting's chief exception.

options.label: Impossible; Category IV is the box for refusing claims
options.consequence: Matches The Crossing and the live rule. Category IV survives as the Accord's box for refusing fraudulent applications, the closing 'Do not file a Category IV application' turns grimly literal, and Codex I's aphorism on raising the dead is recast to match.

options.label: Possible but unauthorised, as now
options.consequence: Contradicts The Crossing unless the texts stay one school's reading. Resurrection becomes something a table can chase, and the Heresiology's case against counterfeit resurrection weakens.

options.label: Forbidden on paper, secretly his own path
options.consequence: Fits the cult of his undeath, but makes the text unreliable, so every mechanic in it needs a canon check before use.

questions.rec_reason: It agrees with The Crossing and the live rule while keeping the text honest; the book stays a warning, and his later lichdom reads as irony, not hypocrisy.
questions.evidence: The Crossing 87-88; R60-04; Heresiology 97, 170; Necrocursica 181, 497; Volume the First 85

questions.title: Does the treatise discuss lichdom?
questions.question: Should the Necrocursica mention liches, the one kind of dead that stays itself, which its author later becomes?
questions.context: The treatise sorts the dead into residues and revenants ('The revenant does not think. It is not the deceased.') but never names a dead person still himself. Canon names liches as the exception to permanent death. Malphas 'did not seek out a lichdom in the conventional sense', and his Golden Remnant, the vessel holding part of his Essence Core, is explicitly unlike 'a phylactery in the old stories'.

options.label: Silent, deliberately
options.consequence: His own fate is the hole in his system. Elegant, but readers may take it for an oversight in a treatise on the dead.

options.label: A core passage filing phylactery lichdom with old stories
options.consequence: Half right, since his Remnant is no phylactery. If the texts' doctrine becomes system canon, the dismissal clashes with the live rule naming liches as the exception.

options.label: One sealed-edition margin line he refuses to expand
options.consequence: Names liches as the one exception he will not treat, and stops. Honest with canon, no false doctrine, no future-dated layer; the reader sees the gap he is walking toward.

options.label: A lich's later margins correcting his thesis
options.consequence: The one qualified voice corrects himself, but the extant copy then postdates the Becoming and the archive's present.

questions.rec_reason: A living Stage IX man cannot know lichdom from inside. Refusing to discuss it is true to his knowledge, agrees with canon and plants the foreshadow in one line.
questions.evidence: R60-04; Lich page 16, 21; Malphas card 26, 42, 99; Necrocursica 141-145, 181

questions.title: Whose voice governs his writing
questions.question: Which voice governs the converted Necrocursica, the opaque commander of Greyshaft Nine or the dry, confessional writer, and what fills his missing voice block?
questions.context: Every major card needs a voice block (fixed slots: what he notices first, sentence length, contractions, shifts under stress, grief and joy); Malphas's card has none. In the Night's Watch scene he is opaque, reads a forester's life 'the way a man reads a bill of lading', and is bone-dry. The Necrocursica is confessional, warm to Paracelsus, lyrical on the platform, and claims 'honesty is a principle I hold'. Neither uses contractions.

options.label: Two registers, one man
options.consequence: The block sets command as his default and the Necrocursica's candour as his grief and joy shifts, the man before The Mother; contractions never. Trim the chatty tics, keep the confessions, so his fall shows in his voice.

options.label: Conform the text to the coldhouse
options.consequence: Colder and shorter, the humour bone-dry, the confessions cut. Loses the Fifth Corruption's 'treat this document as a confession', the attribution's best payoff.

options.label: The candour is strategy
options.consequence: Every self-accusation is a word chosen for the file, consistent with his naming method, but the whole text turns untrustworthy and the tragedy flattens.

questions.rec_reason: No contractions, dry wit and precision already bridge the two voices, and the Invocation date explains why the warmth is there and why it is gone by Greyshaft Nine.
questions.evidence: R52-03, R52-04; Night's Watch 175, 197, 227; Necrocursica 53, 305, 369; voices.yaml 307-308; book bible 21

questions.title: His part in the Genesio activations
questions.question: What part does Malphas play in the Genesio Activation Sequence, where old traces of the dead were activated to finish their unfinished work?
questions.context: Heresiology Case IV, the Genesio Activation Sequence, ends 'Fermentation Perverted often arrives crowned with achievements', and Malphas's card gives him that exact tell. In the Codex and Papers, Thom runs the activations on Gillus's theory, and Gillus says Noxinus 'wrote the architecture'. The Necrocursica's Category Three: 'This is what Vaughaus Thom replicated at scale.' The Heresiology never names Thom.

options.label: Theorist only: he wrote it, Thom ran it
options.consequence: The Codex and Papers plots stand. The card's tell becomes irony: he wrote the warning for a case that is later his.

options.label: Silent partner: his protocol under Thom's hand and signature
options.consequence: His first Fermentation Perverted work runs through another man's signature, The Mother's method before The Mother. The texts stay unchanged on the surface; one sealed-edition margin line hints it; Case IV becomes his unnamed case.

questions.rec_reason: Canon already hangs Case IV's tell on him, running work under someone else's signature is his canon method, and it seeds The Mother without touching the Codex or Papers plots.
questions.evidence: Heresiology 111-121, 211; Malphas card 45-47; The Mother 43 and How a Culture Works; Necrocursica 173; Papers 255

questions.title: Is it the Arena's forbidden source material?
questions.question: Is the Necrocursica part of the forbidden source material Mu-jin says he and the culprit both studied?
questions.context: In the Arena scene Mu-jin cites marginal notes in the Zettari archives from 'the period before the Accord existed to enforce alchemical law', recording failed Mortalis experiments in enough detail to reconstruct, and says the perpetrator studied 'the same source material I have studied'. The scene's notes make the perpetrator Malphas. The Necrocursica is a sealed, margin-annotated casebook of failures, written while the Accord was still forming.

options.label: Yes: the sealed Necrocursica sits beside the Zettari notes
options.consequence: The speech gains a buried confession: Mu-jin read his friend's book and now describes its use without naming its author. No scene edit.

options.label: No: the Zettari notes are separate and older
options.consequence: No link at the Arena; the Necrocursica stays a sealed book, and the scene's irony stays about method only.

options.label: The Zettari marginal notes are the Necrocursica's own margins
options.consequence: Merges two threads into one document, but changes an originated detail in an archived scene and pulls the Zettari into Malphas's past.

questions.rec_reason: It uses the scene as it stands, fits 'before the Accord existed' to a forming Accord, and pays off the paired authorship at the Arena.
questions.evidence: Arena scene 17, 25, 64; Necrocursica 13, 21, 187; R60-09

sections.title: The new Papers author
sections.intro: Oren Corrant is replaced by someone we invent. These questions set who they are and how their field notes read.

questions.title: What record the new author gets
questions.question: How fully should the new Papers author be built: a full character card, a roster NPC, or a named role inside the Papers only?
questions.context: The author writes one of the five canon documents, appears in Mu-jin's Codex III (delivers Gillus's letter, pauses in his doorway), investigates the Genesio and Tempus case and meets Gillus. House rules: a person who matters gets a name; every card carries a pronunciation line, a header dated to a stated moment and, if major, a voice block. Among the authors only Mu-jin has a casting (narration voice) entry.

options.label: Full character card
options.consequence: Fracture of Worlds loadout (the stat sheet), voice block, pronunciation line, dated header, voice fingerprint and casting entry. Most work; the investigator becomes a playable NPC with counters, and the Papers and Codex III share one fixed voice.

options.label: Roster NPC through the NPC build
options.consequence: Want, refusal line, lie, physical inventory and voice, plus a short loadout line. Lighter and upgradable, but with no voice block the Papers and Codex III can drift apart.

options.label: A named role inside the Papers only
options.consequence: Name and office, nothing else. Cheapest, but a canon document's author has no want, voice or limits, and Codex III's portrait has nothing to check against.

questions.rec_reason: The author carries a whole canon text and a scene in Mu-jin's Codex; a card fixes one voice across both, gives the Gillus meeting stakes, and suits the narration pipeline.
questions.evidence: R50-27, R50-34, R52-03, R54-11; Papers 3-25; Codex III docx 18, 350; casting.yaml 884

questions.title: The new author's office
questions.question: What canon office does the new author hold, since 'Enforcer-Archivist' straddles two rival Accord Divisions?
questions.context: The Papers sign 'Enforcer-Archivist, Guild Accord, Research Archives Division', and Codex III calls the author 'an Accord archivist'. Canon: Enforcement (its Sealwrights close cases and seal Crystals) and Research and Archives are separate Divisions in opposing voting blocs; trace examiners read a working's traces as evidence; the crown's Night Watch Society investigates illegal magic. Halveth, the author's supervisor, sits in Research.

options.label: A field archivist of the Research and Archives Division
options.consequence: Drop 'Enforcer'. Halveth and the Division frame stay, Codex III's 'Accord archivist' already fits, and eleven years of contamination sites and relic quarantines read as archive fieldwork, with Enforcement doing the sealing.

options.label: An Enforcement Sealwright seconded to Research
options.consequence: Keeps the enforcer edge, and the rivalry between the two voting blocs becomes texture in every entry. Halveth's authority over a Sealwright needs a line.

options.label: A Night Watch Society investigator on the crown's warrant
options.consequence: Sets the Papers against the power The Mother watches most closely. Halveth's frame becomes a crown office, and the planned book's rule that no file names Malphas binds the Papers too.

questions.rec_reason: Least disruption: a canon Division, Halveth's frame stands, Codex III's own word 'archivist' fits, and the Papers already read as fieldwork rather than enforcement.
questions.evidence: Guild Accord in the Modern Era, section III; R60-11; Gate page, section V; The Night Watch 21; Papers 3, 17-19, 241, 285; Codex III docx 18, 72

questions.title: The new author's culture and naming
questions.question: Which culture does the new author come from, and so which naming convention (how that people builds a name) does the name follow?
questions.context: The Papers are signed from the Division's Urbis office, and the author meets the Trans-Alftian country as a newcomer, 'retracing a route I had only read about'. Canon naming: Concord humans use a small given-name pool plus bynames frozen into surnames; Yukari rename at each life stage; Mahuo put the lineage first with a generation syllable. The Accord files everyone as given name, family, culture and rank, which flattens longer forms. 'Oren Corrant' and 'Osric Salter' are Concord-built.

options.label: Concord human: small name pool, byname surname
options.consequence: An Urbis native named in the Oren Corrant mould, so the filing needs no flattening and name, office and chancery frame agree. Contrasts with Mu-jin's Mahuo name.

options.label: Yukari: Japanese life-stage names
options.consequence: The Accord's four fields cut a layered name down, so every signature shows the filing's cost. Suits a Ketsuen setting if the geography seam places the region there, but the newcomer lines then need a reason.

options.label: Mahuo: Mu-jin's own Korean-register culture
options.consequence: The author shares Mu-jin's naming culture, a quiet bond under Codex III's doorway scene. The Papers need a line on why a Mahuo scholar serves in Urbis, and the two names must not echo.

questions.rec_reason: The text already reads the region as a stranger from Urbis, the Papers' old name is Concord-built, and the Accord's filing takes it cleanly, so nothing new needs explaining.
questions.evidence: R20-1 naming anchors; R23-2 strata; R20-4 filing convention; Papers 3, 39, 241, 286; book bible 167

questions.title: The new author's Stage, or none
questions.question: Is the new Papers author a practitioner, and if so at what Stage (rung of the sixteen-step Temperance ladder)?
questions.context: The author has handled contamination sites, quarantines, two unsanctioned Domain events and a Stage VI claimant, yet samples a floor with a resonance disc for 'the Accord facility' to analyse, has the Tempus drift verified by an observation post, and writes 'Rooms, in my experience, do not have opinions.' Gillus, met alone on a platform, is Stage VII, Mortalis primary, and unusually sensitive to signatures.

options.label: No Stage: unwoken, reading by instrument
options.consequence: Class Ø (a Crystal never woken). Every reading comes from instruments and other people's senses; the Gillus meeting is real risk; a Mother culture finds no signature of theirs to follow. The card needs no Wellsprings.

options.label: Low Stage (III to V) with a trained reading sense
options.consequence: A field examiner whose Crystal helps read residue, with a hard range and a cost; the resonance-disc and 'rooms have no opinions' lines are rewritten to fit.

options.label: Middle Stage (VI to VIII), able to face Gillus
options.consequence: Near-equal to Gillus; the Papers gain workings on the page and lose their reliance on instruments, and the Domain events become things the author handled in person.

questions.rec_reason: The text already has the author reading only by instrument and borrowed senses; knowledge stays honestly limited, and the one meeting with a Stage VII Mortalis practitioner carries real danger.
questions.evidence: Papers 19, 25, 49, 51, 257; Codex III docx 50; Core Vocabulary, Class Ø; The Mother, Relations; Temperance Stages

questions.title: House style of the Papers
questions.question: Which house style should the converted Papers follow: Accord chancery, the writer's own voice, or both in layers?
questions.context: A live rule gives each institution's documents a house style: 'Accord chancery formal and Latinate', 'letters in the writer's voice'. The Papers already split: a classified header, cross-references and a closing note in office form, and entries that are wry and personal because Halveth ordered 'not a report. Actual observations.'

options.label: Two layers: chancery frame, personal entries
options.consequence: Header, classification, cross-references and closing note in formal Latinate chancery; the entries stay in the author's voice. Halveth's order justifies the split, and few edits follow.

options.label: All chancery
options.consequence: Formal and Latinate throughout; the wit and the pharmacologist's 'room hasn't finished' passage flatten into report prose. A heavy rewrite.

options.label: All personal
options.consequence: The chancery frame goes; classification and closing note become the author's asides. Breaks the house-style rule for an Accord-filed document.

questions.rec_reason: The text is already built this way; the rule is met where the Accord speaks, and the author's voice survives where Halveth asked for it.

questions.title: Citing a sealed text without clearance
questions.question: The author is 'not yet cleared' for the sealed Necrocursica yet cites its content twice; how should the converted Papers account for that?
questions.context: The case file holds the sealed Necrocursica, 'which I am not yet cleared for'; Halveth has applied for access. Later entries cite 'what the Necrocursica describes as the Sympathetic Bond Trace' and say 'the Necrocursica is correct that the word matters'. Codex II, which the author is cleared for, reports that residue and quotes the footnote 'Never claim it is the soul.' The header lists the Volitional Trace as 'unverified'.

options.label: Through the Codex: add 'as the Codex reports'
options.consequence: Two phrase edits. The author knows the sealed book only second-hand, which fits the header's 'unverified' Volitional Trace and keeps knowledge limited.

options.label: Clearance arrives mid-file
options.consequence: A dated line records Halveth's request granted before the first citing entry; the author then reads the sealed edition, four residue categories included, and later entries may use them.

options.label: Reads it uncleared and admits it
options.consequence: A breach on the record that Halveth notes in the margin; gives the author a lie or secret for the card, and Gillus a lever.

questions.rec_reason: Smallest edit, consistent with the header, and it keeps the investigator's knowledge honestly partial: what the sealed book says reaches the author only through the Codex.
questions.evidence: Papers 5-7, 23, 57, 139; Codex II docx 99, 103

sections.title: Wellsprings
sections.intro: Where the texts' Wellsprings drift from the Sixty, and what Mortalis and Anamnesis actually are.

questions.title: Which current each Great Work stage draws on
questions.question: Should each of the Great Work's seven stages (alchemy's curriculum) be tied to one of the Sixty Wellsprings (the standing currents that carry the world's laws)?
questions.context: Vol I says each Corruption is a stage 'severed from its Wellspring root', but canon maps few. Alchemetrica's operations table: Coagulation mirrors Coagulatio, Distillation mirrors 'Distillatio' (not one of the Sixty), Conjunction has 'no single Wellspring mirror' and runs on Attraction (the force of recognition and bonds). Dissolution is itself a current. Separation and Fermentation have none; K6 settles Calcination and Distillation. The Heresiology calls the stages 'disciplines imposed upon both matter and maker'. Mu-jin's card harmonises Coagulatio, Distillatio, Fixatio and Calcination, so it follows whatever map is chosen.

options.label: Six stages mapped by physics; Conjunction stays Attraction-driven
options.consequence: Calcination to Cinerion (pyrolytic char), Dissolution to Dissolution, Separation to Judicium (discernment), Fermentation to Rebirthine (breakdown pays for growth), Distillation to Sublimare (if K5 keeps the physics), Coagulation to Coagulatio. Conjunction's Corruption injures Attraction itself. Alchemetrica gains a stage table; Mu-jin's card follows.

options.label: All seven mapped, Conjunction to Manganthra
options.consequence: As A, but Conjunction mirrors Manganthra (catalysis that holds incompatible reactants together). This overrides Alchemetrica's 'no single Wellspring mirror' line outright and puts a current where canon puts the Parunic mediation glyphs.

options.label: Stages are procedures; the root is each working's own current
options.consequence: No stage table. 'Wellspring root' means whatever current a given working draws, as the Heresiology's 'disciplines imposed upon both matter and maker' reads. Vol I's line is reworded, canon is untouched, and the Corruptions get no fixed current.

options.label: Only canon's existing mirrors
options.consequence: Dissolution and Coagulation keep their currents; the other five stay pure procedure. Least change and the weakest tie between alchemy and the Sixty: five of the Seven Corruptions have no current to injure.

questions.rec_reason: Only existing currents, Alchemetrica's Conjunction line kept, every Corruption given a current to injure. Mu-jin's Caloria undertone fits Cinerion; Rebirthine gives Malphas's own Corruption, Fermentation, a current. If K6 makes Calcination and Distillation currents, they mirror themselves.
questions.evidence: Alchemetrica 23-31, 96-104, 108-140; Heresiology 42-47; Vol I wiki 165; Caloria 42, 56-57; Vectoria 49; Vitalia 42; FOW V 48; Mu-jin card 43, 48; Malphas card 45

questions.title: The Genesio site's rung, and why it pushed
questions.question: What rung is the Genesio Anamnesis site on canon's sites ladder, and why did heavy drawing make it push instead of fade?
questions.context: Vol III's climax is a mountain hollow where Anamnesis (the current that reads the past) pools; Thom's coarse drawing made it 'push' and Tempus, a celestial body, drifted. The Heresiology files Genesio under Fermentation Perverted, Malphas's own Corruption. Canon: a drawn site falls or gives out; a site under Obsession Force (a current that takes instead of recognising) stands one rung higher. Standing in a Riptide needs A-grade output; a Whirlpool (Veil-Thin, 'time wrong') S to SS; a Fountainhead (Wellspring Core) SSS.

options.label: Riptide, turned to Obsession Force by Thom's draw
options.consequence: Clean, it needs A-grade output; while Thom draws it reads Whirlpool, so standing there needs S to SS, and 'time wrong' and the Tempus drift (correspondence, not energy) last only while it takes. Completing the oldest Trace drops it a rung.

options.label: Whirlpool, turned to Obsession Force by Thom's draw
options.consequence: Time runs wrong even when clean; corrupted, it reads Fountainhead, so standing there at the height of Thom's work needs SSS output. Mu-jin's visit must fall late in his career under K1, and few others in the texts could enter.

options.label: Whirlpool, clean; the push is pooled, unfinished Traces
options.consequence: The site itself falls as drawn, per canon. Each Trace Thom woke and left unfinished pools in the region like battlefield residue, matching the Heresiology's 'regional saturation through repeated retrieval'. The counter is finishing the pooled Traces, not healing the site.

options.label: Leave it unplaced, like Halloway Mire
options.consequence: Recorded as a site with no density the ladder can read. Cheapest, but nobody can say who may safely stand there, and the push has a reason only in prose.

questions.rec_reason: Only Obsession Force makes a drawn site push; the Heresiology ties the Tempus drift to 'repeated pressure', so it should end with the corruption; completion is a findable counter; a Riptide avoids an Old World Core and an SSS gate.
questions.evidence: Tier Ladders 440-482, 500; Eight Families 106, 131; Heresiology 158, 171, 211-212; Malphas card 45-47; Vol III docx 136, 142

questions.title: Mortalis: river of the dead, or gate
questions.question: In the rewritten texts, is Mortalis the river the dead travel down, or the gate where a living body stops holding itself together?
questions.context: Codex II calls Mortalis 'a river, not a reservoir' and says its 'residual current' animates the impression-body (the temporary likeness of the dead); Vol I calls practice 'a loan' from it. Canon's Vitalia page: life is constant spending, death the return to equilibrium. The Archon Auren, 'Keeper of the Still Gate', holds Mortalis, and Auren's Mortalis working 'opens a threshold, it can't create death'. The river of souls is the Titan Sylorin's, a Pantheon image outside the Sixty. Canon never says Mortalis powers animation.

options.label: Gate, recast to the physics
options.consequence: Mortalis is Auren's Still Gate; the river becomes Sylorin's soulstream, a Pantheon image, not a current. The 'loan' becomes a current borrowed and stepped out of, as Malphas's card says. The sealed vessel holds the impression-body. Rewrites Codex II's Mortalis passages and Corrant 189.

options.label: Keep the river as older hermetic language
options.consequence: The imagery stays, framed as a pre-physics register the author knows is metaphor. Least rewriting, but readers may take it as mechanism, it collides with Sylorin's river, and the 'residual current' animation needs its own disclaimer.

options.label: Extend canon: Mortalis gains a sustaining current
options.consequence: Add a necromantic sustain to Vitalia's Mortalis entry. Truest to the old texts, but it writes new canon, must pass the no-new-mechanism check (R18-2), and gives the made dead a power source the Crossing never grants.

questions.rec_reason: It ties the texts to canon that already exists (the Pantheon, Vitalia's physics, the Heresiology's 'it governs passage') and invents nothing. Malphas, standing in Mortalis since the Becoming, can write the gate from the far side of it.
questions.evidence: Vitalia 48-51; FOW V 98; Heresiology 170; Codex Pantheon (Auren, Sylorin); Spell Index 'The Still Gate's Mercy'; Codex II docx 31, 103; Vol I wiki 85; Malphas card 51-54

questions.title: Anamnesis: keeper of the past, or its reader
questions.question: Does the Anamnesis Wellspring itself store the past, or is it the instrument that reads a past already stored in objects and ground?
questions.context: Vol I says Anamnesis 'holds memory because nothing that has been is erased'; the Corrant Papers call it 'a storage system'. Vol III half-denies this ('does not store memories') yet says it 'keeps the record' of commitments. Canon's Limina page: objects store their history, Anamnesis 'is the instrument, not the miracle', and it fails by erasing a record in the act of reading it. Places hold Mnemata (their memory imprint). Mu-jin's card: he 'reads inherited intention'. Vol III's plot turns on where the record lives.

options.label: Instrument: records live in the ground; Anamnesis reads them
options.consequence: Genesio's Traces are the hollow's Mnemata, and Anamnesis reads and wakes them. Thom's harm is erasure by coarse reading plus the site's corruption. Vol I's 'nothing is erased' stands as the young author's error that Vol III corrects; the Vol III title follows.

options.label: Keeper: amend canon so Anamnesis also preserves
options.consequence: The texts stay nearly intact, but Limina's 'instrument, not the miracle' and the Veil page change, and the canon failure mode (erasing by reading) loses its bite.

options.label: Leave it as in-world theory
options.consequence: No text changes; each author's claim is marked as hypothesis. Canon and the texts keep disagreeing, and every Genesio scene needs its own ruling.

questions.rec_reason: It matches Mu-jin's card and the Codex glyphs Echo-Scar and Sediment, which put the record in the place; canon's own failure mode supplies Thom's harm; the Heresiology's 'charged records' stay true as records held at the site.
questions.evidence: Limina 63-66; Veil 73, 76; Magical Categories 184-188; Heresiology 171; Glyph Index Echo-Scar, Sediment; Mu-jin card 48; Vol III docx 112; Corrant 207, 211, 251; Vol I wiki 117

questions.title: What becomes of the 'Anamnetic fabric'
questions.question: The texts describe an 'Anamnetic fabric', a world-wide memory record the dead dissolve into. Canon has no such medium. What should the rewritten texts do with it?
questions.context: 'Anamnetic' appears about 25 times in the Necrocursica and Vol III and nowhere else in canon. Malphas has the dead dissolve 'back into the Anamnetic fabric of the Continuum'. Canon keeps records in places and objects (their Mnemata, the memory a place holds), gives the cosmic ledger of lived experience to the Archon Maelor, and sends the dead three ways at the Crossing (the parting at death): Echo to the Soul Plane, Temperance Residue to the Wellspring, Name-record to the Archive of Names.

options.label: Recast to canon and drop the term
options.consequence: Records are the Mnemata of places the dead touched; the world-ledger is Maelor's. The Necrocursica's account of death follows the Crossing's three destinations. About 25 lines change; 'Anamnetic activation' becomes 'waking a Trace' or similar.

options.label: Keep it as a scholar's name for all sites' Mnemata
options.consequence: The prose rhythm survives with one in-world coinage, glossed at first use as the sum of every site's Mnemata, not a medium. The dead still part by the Crossing, so the 'dissolve into the fabric' line is recast.

options.label: Make it canon: a Continuum-wide record
options.consequence: New cosmology read through Anamnesis. It must pass the no-new-category check (R18-2), collides with Maelor's ledger, and contradicts the Instrument answer to WS4.

questions.rec_reason: Canon already has the words (Mnemata, Maelor's ledger, the Crossing), a precise diagnostician like Mu-jin would use them, and a coinage invites readers to hunt for a medium that does not exist.
questions.evidence: Necrocursica 85, 357, 397; Vol III docx 112, 136, 204, 248; Limina 64; Veil 73; Magical Categories 184-188; Codex Pantheon Sylorin row (Maelor); Crossing 22-34

sections.title: Death, residues and the made dead
sections.intro: How the texts' account of what the dead leave behind connects to The Crossing and the Soul Crystal, and what builds an impression-body.

questions.title: Which Soul Crystal layer each residue comes from
questions.question: Should the rewritten texts tie each residue a dead practitioner leaves to one of the Soul Crystal's three layers, and by which map?
questions.context: The residues never name a layer (Essence Core: identity, memory; Aether Shell: outward force; Attraction Layer: bonds, harmonisations). Canon supports a map: Harmonic Imprint = a place's Mnemata (memory imprint); Sympathetic Bond Trace = Attraction Layer bonds; Parunic Echo = Aetheric Residue (a working's trace); Corporeal Residue = the body carrying the Temperance Residue (the Stages and harmonisations a life earned) nine days; Aetheric Shell = the Shell; Nospheric Echo = the Crossing's Echo (Core) held back, though its place-half duplicates the Harmonic Imprint.

options.label: Use the map; split the Nospheric Echo
options.consequence: Every residue lands on a layer and a Crossing product. The Nospheric Echo narrows to the held Echo (voice, habit, possession); its place-imprint half moves to the Harmonic Imprint. K4 decides whether the Crossing page gains the map.

options.label: Use the map; keep the Nospheric Echo whole
options.consequence: Same map, but the overlap stands as two authors naming one thing twice (Mu-jin's Harmonic Imprint, Malphas's Nospheric Echo). Less rewriting of Malphas's chapter; a careful reader finds the duplicate.

options.label: No map; each author keeps his own vocabulary
options.consequence: Least work, but the residues float free of the Soul Crystal, the opposite of what the conversion is for.

questions.rec_reason: It ties every residue to a layer using existing canon only and removes the one real duplicate. The Volitional Trace is left out on purpose: its home is DE3.
questions.evidence: Core Vocabulary 28-30, 40, 58-60, 107; Crossing 22-34, 112-113; Veil 73, 78; FOW V 142-157; Codex II wiki 82-84; Necrocursica 97-109

questions.title: What a practitioner's body holds after nine days
questions.question: The Necrocursica says a powerful practitioner's body stays active for years; canon says nine days, then 'meat'. After nine days, what does the body still hold?
questions.context: Malphas's text: the Corporeal Residue lasts 'hours in Stage I practitioners to years in Stage VII and above', and such bones are 'still doing something, decades after death'. The Crossing: the Temperance Residue (the Stages and harmonisations a life earned) diffuses out through the body in nine days, varying with Stage in ways never measured, then 'what remains is meat'. Yet the Alchemical Index grades practitioner grave-dirt and Crystal-bearer bone-ash Class IV (identity-shaped material) with no time limit, and Trait tissue lays Traits into bone.

options.label: Only Trait tissue: passive Class IV carry, no active residue
options.consequence: Stage stretches the nine days by days, not years. The Crossing's 'meat' reads as 'no Temperance left', and the ledger stands. Malphas's decades-old bones survive as passive Trait carry: old graves are Class IV stock, but nothing in them is still diffusing.

options.label: Nothing: restrict the ledger to the nine-day window
options.consequence: The Crossing wins outright. Gravetide Ink's and Granite-Bone Mortar's Class IV grades apply only inside nine days, and the decades line is cut. The cleanest death law, but it reprices two canon materials and the grave-dirt trade.

options.label: Keep years, as Malphas's own measurement
options.consequence: He claims to have measured the Stage variance canon calls uncharacterised. If true in-world, high-Stage graves keep live Temperance for years, rendering houses dig them up, and the Crossing, the Standing Index and the Rites all need amending.

questions.rec_reason: It reconciles both canon pages without repricing anything, keeps the nine-day law the Class IV trade rests on, and lets Malphas's eerie decades-old bones stand as Trait carry rather than living Essence.
questions.evidence: Crossing 52-54, 73, 137; Rites 57; Alchemical Index 63, 68, 111; Standing Index 29; Core Vocabulary 107; Necrocursica 97, 133

questions.title: Where an unfinished decision goes at death
questions.question: What is the Accord's leading account of where an unfinished decision (the Volitional Trace) goes when its maker dies?
questions.context: If you take K6's recommended answer, the Trace stays contested, so this picks the reading the Accord teaches, with a rival reading voiced in the texts. The Trace drives all three Codex volumes, the Necrocursica's Category III and the Corrant Papers; no canon category holds it. Codex III: Traces fade over 'decades, sometimes generations'; Genesio's is 260 years old, left by a practitioner who died beside the site. Canon homes: the Plane of Fate (the Attraction Layer's plane) records 'bonds, oaths, grudges'; a vow is a standing law in the Essence Core; the Heresiology's Anamnesis holds 'charged records of lived commitment'. The Temperance Residue returns only to Wellsprings the person harmonised.

options.label: A commitment laid into the place, read by Anamnesis
options.consequence: An Attraction Layer commitment settles into the ground where the person was bound, as Mnemata (a place's memory imprint). It lasts where ground holds records well (an Anamnesis site like Genesio) and fades elsewhere; Anamnesis reads and wakes it. No canon page changes.

options.label: An open oath on the Plane of Fate
options.consequence: The Trace is an unclosed entry among the Plane of Fate's recorded oaths, reachable wherever the Veil thins. It works anywhere, not just at Anamnesis sites, but weakens the plot's reason to be at Genesio.

options.label: A fourth product of the Crossing
options.consequence: The Codex's 'fourth residue' becomes literally a fourth thing that parts at death. Strong drama, but the Crossing page is incomplete unless it stays a disputed thesis the Accord has not accepted.

options.label: A vow held in the Essence Core, gone with the Echo
options.consequence: The Trace is Core law and leaves for the Soul Plane within hours. It uses canon's vow mechanic, but any contact becomes retrieval of the soul, against the Heresiology's 'the trace is not the soul' and the Codex's 'impression, not retrieval'.

questions.rec_reason: It pairs with the Instrument answer, matches the Heresiology and Mu-jin's card, and explains why a Trace left beside Genesio survived 260 years where others faded. The 'fourth product' can stay the authors' argument.
questions.evidence: Core Vocabulary 29, 48, 60; Heresiology 170-171, 238; Crossing 28, 32, 52-53; Vol III docx 112-116, 160, 194-220; Necrocursica 109, 357; Corrant 251

questions.title: Which summoning layers make an impression-body
questions.question: Which of canon's summoning layers build an impression-body (the eleven-day likeness of the dead), given the Codex's own Aphorism that the maker 'summons himself'?
questions.context: No canon page says how one is built. The Spirit Summoning Arts call every spirit 'a lawful extrusion of the summoner's own Soul Crystal' and split the work: Arts builds the vessel (often alchemical; Stage VII anchored, IX independent), Animatria shapes identity from the summoner's own Core, Vocatia (summoning by recognition; Stage X for stable contact) reaches a presence outside him, Binding sets how long it lasts. The Codex's Aphorism: the maker 'summons himself, arranged in their image'. Paracelsus's body lasted eleven days and finished Madeleine's decision.

options.label: A Vocatia call on an Arts vessel, Binding-sealed
options.consequence: The Trace or the mourner's bond is the channel, so something outside the maker answers, which is why the body acted on its own. The Aphorism loosens: he summoned neither the departed nor himself. Stage X floor for stable contact.

options.label: An Animatria construct on an Arts vessel
options.consequence: The maker's own Core, shaped from the site's record into her likeness: the Aphorism becomes literal mechanics, Stage VII floor. But nothing outside him answers, so the Corrant ending, the body completing her decision, must be recast as his reading acted out.

options.label: A Greater Summons: vessel, Animatria and Vocatia together
options.consequence: Canon's Tier III (Stage IX to XI, 'ancestral echoes'): Arts vessel, the maker's Core as identity, Vocatia contact with the Trace. The Aphorism turns literal; the Trace explains what he did not foresee. Eleven days outruns 'minutes to hours', so vessel and Binding carry it.

options.label: A Draft from Class IV remains, no summons
options.consequence: An alchemical work with Class, Fidelity and Carry; identity-shaped Carry explains 'knew the names'. Needs grave-dirt, bone-ash or a Crystal-bearer's blood, and nothing says Madeleine bore a Crystal. No one answers, so the Corrant ending must be recast.

questions.rec_reason: It is canon's own recipe for an ancestral echo, makes the Codex's Aphorism literal, keeps the Corrant ending, and uses Vocatia, the Mahuo art Mu-jin trained in, so he can write it from the inside.
questions.evidence: Spirit Summoning Arts 13, 21-23, 30-49, 60-67; Crossing 87; Codex II wiki 32-35; Corrant 131-139, 171-181; Heresiology 210; Mu-jin card 48

questions.title: Is the impression-body's vessel a graded Draft
questions.question: Is the vessel Paracelsus built at his bench a graded Draft (an alchemical product marked for Class, Fidelity and Carry), and must it contain the dead?
questions.context: Alchemetrica's Twelve Turnings end in the Mark: Class, Fidelity, Carry. Class IV material (rendered from something that carried a Soul Crystal) carries identity: practitioner grave-dirt and Crystal-bearer bone-ash grade Class IV, and R54-42 makes a living Crystal-bearer's blood Class IV. The Bench of Attribution names the class, never the source. Nothing in the texts says Madeleine Ault bore a Crystal, and she died two years before the commission. The Summons ladder prices a call by its cost; the Bench prices a Draft.

options.label: Graded Draft; Class IV only when rendered remains go in
options.consequence: The vessel carries Class, Fidelity, Carry and a price. Ordinary commissions use Class I to III stock; Thom's regional scaling uses Class IV, where the Bench's blind spot on source and the black market bite.

options.label: Summoning infrastructure, never Marked
options.consequence: The vessel is Arts work priced only as a call cost on the Summons ladder. Simplest ledger, but Paracelsus's bench becomes set dressing and alchemy's tie to the made dead weakens.

options.label: Graded Draft that always needs Class IV
options.consequence: Every impression-body consumes the dead or a Crystal-bearing mourner's blood. Carry explains 'knew the names' outright; commissions become a Class IV trade the Bench cannot trace, and Madeleine or Cassian must be ruled a Crystal-bearer.

questions.rec_reason: Paracelsus's bench makes it a Draft, which ties alchemy to summoning; Class IV stays optional because Madeleine is no known Crystal-bearer; Thom's scaling fits the Heresiology's 'regional saturation through repeated retrieval'.
questions.evidence: Alchemetrica 110-140; Standing Index 29, 49, 54; Alchemical Index 63, 68; R54-42; Bench of Attribution 68; Tier Ladders 310, 343-350; Codex II docx 27; Heresiology 171

questions.title: Whether a revenant happens without a necromancer
questions.question: Can a revenant (a dead body that moves without thinking) arise on its own, without a necromancer, and by what canon mechanism?
questions.context: The Necrocursica says a revenant forms when the residues meet a still-active Aether Shell early after death, 'not a supernatural phenomenon', and that it 'does not think'. Canon's walking dead are bodies whose three Crossing products were 'prevented from parting'. Necromancy does that on purpose; a body denied its nine days where the Wellspring cannot reach yields 'a lawful Echo with nowhere to go'; battlefield residue that cannot diffuse pools; and 'a haunting is a charge with no path'.

options.label: A Crossing that stalls on its own
options.consequence: A revenant is a body that spends its nine days where the Wellspring cannot take the residue: sealed ground, saturated battlefields. It fades when diffusion completes; moving or grounding the body (Stillgate Ash) is the counter. Malphas's 'not supernatural' becomes the Crossing's own account.

options.label: Only through necromancy
options.consequence: The strictest reading of the Crossing. The Necrocursica's natural revenant is cut, and the Bestiary's taint-born and restless undead need a separate explanation.

options.label: Keep the Necrocursica's mechanism
options.consequence: A third undead mechanism beside necromancy and taint, resting on an 'active Aetheric Shell' after death that canon never defines. Revenant scenes then need two rules.

questions.rec_reason: It uses the Rites and the Crossing's battlefield pooling, gives a counter someone can find, and keeps Malphas's line nearly word for word. The Tria Prima of the dead stays his alchemical gloss.
questions.evidence: Necrocursica 129-145; Undying and Constructs 14, 24, 49; Crossing 88, 92-93, 126; Rites 86; Alchemical Index 46

questions.title: Whether 'necromancy' stays the texts' word
questions.question: Canon's necromancy only holds a body's parting products together. Should the rewritten texts still call impression-body work 'necromantic'?
questions.context: The Crossing defines necromancy narrowly: holding the three products (Echo, Temperance Residue, Name-record) together after they should part; summoning the dead is 'a different discipline governed elsewhere'. A commission two years after a death cannot be necromancy in that sense. The Codex calls the impression 'what the necromantic tradition calls retrieval'; the Necrocursica is a 'Treatise on Cadaverous Alchemy'; the Heresiology itself says 'Necromantic Manuscript' loosely. Mu-jin's card makes him a precise diagnostician.

options.label: Keep it as the scholars' loose word, with one legal note
options.consequence: Both authors use 'necromantic' as the period term, and the Necrocursica adds a line that the Accord's legal sense is narrower. Matches the Heresiology's own loose usage; least rewriting.

options.label: Split by author: Mu-jin precise, Malphas loose
options.consequence: Mu-jin's Codex names the work as summoning and cites 'necromantic' only as the tradition's word; Malphas's treatise keeps it freely. Adds a voice difference between the authors and a small sweep of the Codex.

options.label: Replace it throughout with summoning and Mortalis terms
options.consequence: The strictest canon fit, but it loses period flavour, and the Necrocursica's subtitle and the Heresiology's 'Necromantic Manuscript' case need renaming.

questions.rec_reason: Both authors are precise men, and the Necrocursica is exact everywhere else (its glyph chains, its Mechanica). Making Malphas the loose one splits his voice. One legal note keeps The Crossing's narrow sense honest.
questions.evidence: Crossing 87-88; Codex II docx 31; Alftian Codex meta page 57; Necrocursica 3; Heresiology 127, 209; Mu-jin card 43, 48

sections.title: The Great Work and the corruptions
sections.intro: How the seven alchemical stages and their corruptions connect to the Temperance ladder, the workshop's Turnings and a character sheet.

questions.title: Great Work stages against the Temperance ladder
questions.question: Should the Great Work's seven stages map onto the sixteen Temperance Stages, and if so, how?
questions.context: Volume I calls the Great Work (the seven alchemical stages, Calcination to Coagulation) 'the Temperance path itself'; Volume II sends the stages 'toward the Temperance Stages' (the sixteen rungs of a soul's reorganisation under pressure). Canon never pairs them. The Heresiology makes the stages disciplines of 'matter and maker'; Alchemetrica says a pure alchemist (Class Ø, a Crystal that never woke) cannot temper and hardens by the Weathering (grain) instead. Read literally, the Codex puts pure alchemists on a ladder they cannot climb.

options.label: Parallel disciplines, no stage-for-stage match
options.consequence: Volume I's appendix line and Volume II's 'Temperance Stages' sentence are rewritten so the Work runs alongside Temperance. Agrees with the Heresiology, leaves pure alchemists untouched, adds no mechanics, and gives alchemy its weakest link to the system.

options.label: The double seven, with a grain clause for Class Ø
options.consequence: Stages I-VII walk the seven once, VIII-XIV again (the Codex's own 'spiral'): Splintering V is Fermentation, Invocation IX Dissolution, Dissonance XI Conjunction, Zenith XIV Coagulation. For Class Ø the maker side is read on grain. A ruling and one line on the Temperance page.

options.label: Mu-jin's school's thesis, argued in-world, possibly wrong
options.consequence: Mu-jin argues the match as his school's reading, a named lens under R48-22; no rule changes and the page may show him wrong. The link to the system stays rhetorical, and pure alchemists are never addressed.

questions.rec_reason: Only B ties the Work to a named mechanism, using the Temperance page's own two seven-Stage phases. It lands on Malphas's card too: his Catalysts fall at Invocation (Dissolution, his primary Wellspring) and Zenith (Coagulation).
questions.evidence: Volume the First 159; Vol II docx 149, 273; Temperance Stages VI:14-17, 47, 63; Heresiology 23, 45; Alchemetrica 80-82; Malphas's card 21-24, 53.

questions.title: Where Fermentation sits against the Rot
questions.question: Given that the bench rots before it weds but the Heresiology joins before it ferments, how should the seven stages line up with the Twelve Turnings?
questions.context: Alchemetrica's Twelve Turnings (the workshop's bench steps) already gloss Burning as calcination, Taking dissolution, Parting separation, Wedding conjunction, Setting congelation. The Rot (putrefaction, six to nine weeks sealed) comes before the Wedding: 'a working that never blacks has not rotted and will not conjoin.' The Heresiology puts Conjunction before Fermentation and calls lawful fermentation 'rot in service to transformation'. The Four Operations are verb-classes; Sublimation (the Rising) has no stage. Cards were already corrected for treating stage or Turning names as Wellsprings.

options.label: The Rot is Fermentation; the two orders differ on purpose
options.consequence: A concordance table in Alchemetrica says so outright: matter rots before it weds, the maker commits before he ferments. Mu-jin gets a teaching line. No page is reordered; the Blacking belongs to Fermentation.

options.label: Fermentation begins in the Rot and completes at the Feeding
options.consequence: Fermentation spans two Turnings: the Rot kills, the Feeding (cibation, measured increments after the Wedding) grows it back. The doctrine counts the stage where it completes, so both orders agree. Same concordance table; nothing reordered.

options.label: Reorder the Heresiology: Fermentation before Conjunction
options.consequence: Breaks the Heresiology's order, its diagnostic table and the Codex's numbering of the corruptions, which follow the stages.

options.label: No concordance; doctrine and bench stay unconnected
options.consequence: No edits. The converted Codex cannot line its alchemy up with the workshop, and readers meet two orders with no explanation.

questions.rec_reason: B makes both canon pages true with nothing to explain away, keeps the Heresiology's order, table and the Codex's numbering intact, and gives the Rot its lawful meaning: death before the thing is remade.
questions.evidence: Alchemetrica 98-104, 110-124 (Turning glosses 113-120), 147-154, 323-330; Heresiology 44, 113, 267-275; Silas, Karasaki, Kytheris card corrections.

questions.title: Where Distillation sits at the bench
questions.question: Since no Turning is a distillation, where at the bench does the doctrine's sixth stage, Distillation, happen?
questions.context: Alchemetrica keeps Distillation as one of the Four Operations (isolation and purification, 'also the forensic operation'), but no Turning is a distillation: the menstruum (solvent) belongs to the Taking and the Rising is sublimation. The colour readings run Blacking (rot), Whitening ('separation complete and the material purified'), Yellowing, Reddening (completion), and a working that skips the Whitening 'has skipped the purification'. The doctrine ends Fermentation, Distillation, Coagulation. Mu-jin is harmonised with Distillatio, so his Codex will say where it happens.

options.label: The Whitening: purification inside the sealed vessel, read by colour
options.consequence: Distillation runs as circulation in the Returner (condensate fed back for weeks unopened) and is read as the Whitening. Blacking, Whitening, Reddening then track Fermentation, Distillation, Coagulation. The concordance pins it to a colour, not a Turning.

options.label: The Reading: Distillation is the forensic assay before the Burning
options.consequence: Distillation becomes the bench's first act, not its sixth. Fits 'the forensic operation' and Mu-jin's diagnostic identity, but bench and doctrine orders split again and the text must say why.

options.label: Before the bench: it prepares the menstruum for the Taking
options.consequence: Distillation becomes a supply operation outside the Turnings. Simple, but it makes the sixth stage of the Work a chore done before the Work begins.

questions.rec_reason: The colour sequence already follows the doctrine's last three stages in order, and canon's own warning about a skipped Whitening is a warning about skipped purification. No Turning is added, so the Twelve stay twelve.
questions.evidence: Alchemetrica 100-104 (Operations), 113-124 (Turnings), 147-156 (colours), Returner in Vessels; Heresiology 44; Mu-jin's card 48, 83, 99.

questions.title: What Sulphur, Salt and Mercury map to
questions.question: Should the Tria Prima (Paracelsus's three principles: active, fixed, mediating) correspond to something in the magic system, and to what?
questions.context: Volume I has Furveus (Paracelsus) split compounds into Sulphur, Salt and Mercury by Spagyria ('Separate. Purify. Recombine.'); the Necrocursica maps them onto three of its residues, calls its triad 'modified', and leaves the Aetheric Shell residue out. Canon has the triad nowhere but 'licensed spagyrists'. It does have triads: the Soul Crystal's three layers (Essence Core on the Soul Plane, Aether Shell on the Material, Attraction Layer on the Fate), and 'reagents are the nouns, the Wellspring the verb, Glyphica the grammar'. The crucible is 'a Soul Crystal analogue'.
