questions.title: What moved Tempus, and its course
questions.question: What caused the Tempus drift, and did it settle, speed up, or reverse?
questions.context: Volume II blames the commission's single Mortalis opening and says the drift 'has stabilised'. Volume III blames rising Anamnesis pressure at Genesio from Thom's activations and says Tempus 'will return to its correct position over the next quarter-year'. The Papers suspect first one, then the other. Heresiology Case V sides with Volume III: 'deviation followed repeated pressure upon a regional metaphysical field'. Mu-jin's Sight Through the Glass reads Wellspring drift locally and forty seconds ahead, not a region over months.

options.label: A sequence; Volume II's cause is Mu-jin's first wrong guess
options.consequence: The commission's nudge settles, then the drift resumes and accelerates with Thom's activations, and reverses once the old Trace completes. Volume III gains one sentence naming the earlier error. Matches Case V and his card's limits.

options.label: Both causes contribute
options.consequence: Both explanations stay true and Case V's 'repeated pressure' covers them, but readers get no correction beat.

options.label: Volume II's cause is right
options.consequence: Volume III's cause and course are rewritten, and so is Heresiology Case V.

questions.rec_reason: Each text stays true at its own date, canon's case wording stands, and a master misreading a regional effect with a local instrument is knowledge that is limited, not omniscient.
questions.evidence: Volume II 221-229, 263; Volume III 86, 142, 310; Corrant 27, 205-211; Heresiology 211-212; Mu-jin's card 96.

questions.title: What physically moved Tempus
questions.question: Is the Tempus drift a mechanical effect with an Essence price, or the Continuum's answer by correspondence, with no energy reaching the planet?
questions.context: Canon names no energy that could move a body in the sky. The Heresiology files Genesio under 'celestial correspondence', and the Codex's closing Correction calls correspondence 'a law of response'. SE8 decides which body Tempus is and SE9 decides the drift's course; this decides the mechanism.

options.label: Correspondence: no energy moves it
options.consequence: The drift is the delayed answer the Codex argues for. Its price is booked as debt on the site and the operators, not as an EU figure.

options.label: A real energy draw from the Genesio site
options.consequence: Needs an EU figure large enough to shift a planet, which the Genesio site cannot plausibly supply.

options.label: Coincidence the Accord misreads
options.consequence: A normal astronomical drift. The texts' argument becomes a scholarly error, and Heresiology Case V becomes a cautionary tale about over-reading.

questions.rec_reason: It keeps the Codex's thesis, needs no impossible number, and matches how the Heresiology already files the case.
questions.evidence: Heresiology 211-212; Alftian Codex overview 71; Vol II docx 223-229

questions.title: God-Essence: force or belief-word
questions.question: Is God-Essence a real force in the world, or the Heralds' religious word for something canon already names?
questions.context: Volume I: God-Essence 'ran through Heraldic structures like blood through limestone veins', and its appendix states 'the structural law of God-Essence correspondence'; Asclepius thinks it 'an embarrassing relic of pre-Accord theology'. Canon has no such doctrine. Omnara, the source of all, is beyond godhood: 'To call Omnara a god would be to diminish it'. The Current, a faith of those living near Wellsprings, holds 'the currents were here first'. Beatrix Vaelthorn's card has 'residual god-essence leakage' killing diggers at the Sirel ruins.

options.label: A belief-word: Wellspring Essence treated as divine
options.consequence: No new metaphysics. Volume I's 'structural law' becomes the Heralds' reading; the humming bridges are ordinary inscribed arrays. If the Heralds serve Maelor, it names Essence as his gift. Sirel's leakage stays a separate folk name.

options.label: Map it to a canon term: Omnara's residue or Archon-law
options.consequence: Gives the doctrine a cosmological root; the term must be chosen and checked against the Epoch register.

options.label: A real, measurable substance, the same as Sirel's leakage
options.consequence: New metaphysics: the Standing Index and Fracture of Worlds need an entry, and Beatrix's card gains a cause.

questions.rec_reason: It keeps the texts' religious flavour and Asclepius's scepticism without adding a force to the magic system, and it sits naturally beside the Current.
questions.evidence: Volume the First 47, 122, 157; Omnara and the Division 25; Faiths of the Four Quarters 60-61; Beatrix Vaelthorn's card 112, 135.

questions.title: What 'the Eressean era' points to
questions.question: Volume III dates the Genesio Wellspring as 'possibly pre-dating the Eressean era'. What should that phrase point to?
questions.context: Canon has no Eressean era. The High Empire of Eresse is dated 'First Eon, Great Spirit War Era', an era with no place on the count. The Concordance's count, the only one under Accord writ, runs from −1,400. Its Antediluvian Calendar (−900 to −450) built cities on top of Wellsprings and drew them to exhaustion; such a site 'stops recognising visitors and begins taking from them'. The Guild surveyed nine and 'declined to publish a finding on what the sites are now doing'.

options.label: The High Empire of Eresse, First Eon
options.consequence: Real depth, but inherits the Great Spirit War Era's unplaced dating.

options.label: The count itself: 'possibly older than reckoned history'
options.consequence: Dated and sealed; claims nothing further about the site.

options.label: An Antediluvian site, worked before that Calendar closed
options.consequence: Genesio becomes one of the Guild's surveyed sources, its old hall built on the Wellspring. The unpublished finding on what those sites 'are now doing' becomes the texts' reason Genesio pushes back when drawn.

options.label: Cut the clause
options.consequence: Loses the only line that shows the Wellspring's age.

questions.rec_reason: It dates by the only count the Accord recognises, and gives Genesio's age, its old hall and its rising pressure a canon history instead of an unplaced elvish era.
questions.evidence: Volume III 122 (Volume the Third 72); High Empire of Eresse 14; Powers of the Imperial Age 91; Concordance 22-24, 60-66, 82-85.

sections.title: Method and output
sections.intro: How the converted texts get written, where they go, and what else in canon changes with them.

questions.title: Wiki pages for the Necrocursica and Papers
questions.question: Should the converted Necrocursica and the new author's Papers become wiki and Notion pages, and where do they sit?
questions.context: Only the three Codex volumes are on the wiki. Volume III and the overview already depend on the Papers' postscript and on Halveth, whom no page describes, and the Necrocursica's Appendix II asks 'File them adjacent'. The Heresiology's (canon's corruption casebook) cases and Malphas's card point at events readers cannot yet read. An 'In-World Documents & the Narrative Archive' section already holds Mu-jin's Zettari–Mahou Accord and his letter to Ara.

options.label: Publish both under The Alftian Codex section
options.consequence: Five pages sit together; Volume III's references and the Halveth line resolve; the INDEX section grows from three pages to five. 'Sealed' and 'Level VI' become in-world labels on public pages.

options.label: Publish both under In-World Documents
options.consequence: They sit with Mu-jin's other in-world papers and link from the Codex overview; 'file them adjacent' is kept by links, not placement.

options.label: Keep them off the wiki
options.consequence: Volume III and the overview are edited so nothing depends on the Papers' postscript or on Halveth; the texts live only as source files.

options.label: Summaries only on the overview
options.consequence: A light touch, but the Heresiology's cases and Malphas's card point at texts nobody can read.

questions.rec_reason: The trilogy already depends on both texts, and the Necrocursica asks to be filed beside it.
questions.evidence: Necrocursica 485 ('File them adjacent'); overview 83-86; Volume III 18, 322, 404; INDEX 277-281; In-World Documents section

questions.title: Card write-back and the renames registry
questions.question: Do Mu-jin's and Malphas's cards absorb the texts' events, and do the renames go into the registry the stale-name sweep uses?
questions.context: The conversion adds the commission, the Genesio hollow and the Codex years to Mu-jin's life, and the Genesio confinement and the treatise to Malphas's; neither card's Lore or Ties says so. The renames registry feeds the stale-name check and the Notion sweep that catch leftover old names. The narration voice file has only Mu-jin. Pages outside the volumes that name the texts include the Lore & History hub, the overview, the Heresiology cases, the Errata page and both cards.

options.label: Write back and register
options.consequence: Both cards gain the events, checked by the lore-writing pass; the registry gains Vis Trismegistus to Kwon Mu-jin (full name only), Oren Corrant to the new author, Noxinus Ren to Malphas if Noxinus goes, and ST1's renames; casting entries follow.

options.label: Write back, hand-edit pages, no registry
options.consequence: The cards stay in step, but leftover old names are likely on the hub, the overview and the Heresiology's cross-references.

options.label: No write-back
options.consequence: The texts stand alone; cards and texts drift apart and the next character-lore pass flags them.

questions.rec_reason: The sweep catches only what the registry lists, and the cards are what every later scene reads.
questions.evidence: build/renames.yaml 1-2; build/casting.yaml 884; Mu-jin's card Lore and Ties; Malphas's card 45, 142; Lore & History hub 15-43; Errata 39

questions.title: Order of work, one document per commit
questions.question: In what order are the five documents converted, given one document per commit?
questions.context: Each text quotes others. Volume II quotes the Necrocursica's footnote; the Papers cite Volumes I and II and the Necrocursica; Volume III cites the Papers; the supplied Necrocursica cites all three volumes and the Papers, so it reads as a later edition. The repo rule is one pack (here, one document) per commit, with a stop and a report at the end of each phase. The doctrine itself (residues, Corruptions) is fixed by this questionnaire before any text is touched.

options.label: Composition order: Volumes I, II, Papers, Volume III, Necrocursica
options.consequence: Each document is converted after everything it quotes, so no conversion cites an unconverted source; the Necrocursica's revised edition comes last and cites the finished four.

options.label: Mechanism first: Necrocursica, then Volumes I to III, then Papers
options.consequence: The doctrine text lands first, but its citations of Volume III and the Papers point at unconverted texts and need a second pass.

options.label: Spine first: Volumes I to III, then Necrocursica and Papers

questions.question: Where does the finished output go: Notion pages, local drafts, fresh docx files for Isaac's folder, or a combination?
questions.context: The repo's wiki folder mirrors Notion through the hourly sync, so a Notion page reaches the wiki on its own. Isaac's standing direction is that Notion publishing happens in-session. His originals are docx files in his true-canon folder, the Volume I docx included, and other in-world documents there, such as Anima Veri Credentis, exist both as docx and as wiki pages. The source docx files are never overwritten.

options.label: Notion pages plus fresh docx files beside the originals
options.consequence: Pages are published in-session and mirrored by the sync; new docx files, such as 'The Alftian Codex (Mu-jin edition)', are saved next to his originals, which stay untouched.

options.label: Notion pages only
options.consequence: One home; his docx folder keeps only the old attributions.

options.label: Local markdown drafts first, Notion after his read
options.consequence: A review stop before publishing; slower, and it runs against the in-session publishing direction.

options.label: Fresh docx files only
options.consequence: His folder is current, but the wiki keeps the old texts and every downstream page stays stale.

The Spirit Rune Arts phoneme table (:100-107) and the Open Crucible (:44, :57, :125) name codes differently from the Master Glyph Index (Ie Insight or Perception, Ma Memory or Recall, Wy Truth or Motion; also Ka, Va, Se, Ae). They also use codes the Index lacks (Ci, Zo, No, Tar, Ky, Si, Zu, Fi). R18-4 makes the Index the authority.

Hiromi card birth order. Hiromi Mahuo :22 and :90 make him Geturo's twin with Lily older. RULINGS.md:518 (Geturo 15 eldest, Hiromi 13, Lily 12) and the card's own :118 disagree. The ruling already settles it, so the row records the card's lag and its fix.

Malphas card As Of against its stats. :18 sets As Of at the Greyshaft Nine coldhouse, where he is still alive: the Becoming comes after the coldhouse (:136; bible.md:32), and his Conversion froze at IX (:79). Yet :62 gives the lich's stats: Stage XIV Zenith, Level 475, Tier of Standing 8.

The Mother before the Becoming. R60-24 (RULINGS.md:2061) makes The Mother 'a religious following of the Becoming'. Yet its Greyshaft Nine coldhouse cell (RULINGS.md:2031; The Mother:58) runs before the Becoming (Malphas card :136).

Monlithion against Monolithion. The Master Codex spells it 'Monlithion' (Lists row 34; Glyph Index [Inr] primary, [Vt] attested; Spell Index 'Inertial Chorus'). FOW V:85 and Eight Families:31 spell it 'Monolithion'. RULINGS.md:318-321 cannot settle this because FOW and the Codex are the two sides. Check 37 flags neither.

A coal boiler against R59-01. Bearing and the Holding :55-57 ('It burns coal') and Four Ceilings :247-249 describe a coal boiler. R59-01 (doc-era-apparatus-law:18, live), Bearing and the Holding :49 and Four Ceilings :243 say nothing burns and there is no steam engine.

Rail in the Voyager Era. Read literally, R53-01 (doc-world-texture-law:19) spreads 1800s technology across the whole Imperial Age. Four Ceilings (:155, :192-194, :275) and Mechanica:65 date the mains and rail to about 315 IC at the earliest. Isaac's settled direction, no rail in the Voyager Era, is the ruling to log.

Errata:39 finds that 'not one of' the Alftian codices 'cites an Age'. Yet wiki Volume the First:14, Volume the Second:14, Volume the Third:235 and the overview :14 all stamp 'Era of Voyagers'. The conversion settles this through K1.

Mu-jin's age on the Ashgate road. RULINGS.md:518 turns 'ten years since' into twenty-four, which makes him 38 at the card's As Of, before Ashgate. Academy State of Play:13 and bible.md:151 put 24 at Hon-guk and 38 at the Academy, although 24 + 13 = 37. Scenes say 'forty years' (10_mujin:73; Arena:13).
Aetheric Residue permanence. Core Vocabulary:40 calls Residue 'A permanent, if often subtle, change'. The Mechanica page :50 says ordinary residue 'thins on a schedule'.

Over-claimed standing. Mu-jin card :163 says a summoner who claims a standing he lacks 'gets nothing'. Counted Speech :110 says an over-warrant seals and is deducted from hands, hearing, teeth or years (:149). Rimward (card :178) sides with the Counted Speech but cost an eye, which :149 does not list.

Pure alchemists' rank. Alchemetrica ranks Crystal-less alchemists at Tier Four (:75, :77), and its 'Dormant Crystal' (:80) contradicts its 'No Soul Crystal' (:66). Tiered Path:15 makes every Tier a Crystal change, VIII:69 puts Dormant at Class Ø pre-Initiate, and X:515 caps items at the maker's Tier of Standing.

The Real Alchemy is missing. R18-5-ALCHEMY_SOURCE_ORDER (pack-18:234-258) makes it one of three required sources, 'none of them optional'. No such page exists in wiki/, in true-canon or in Notion (searched 2026-09-28). C-058 logged only the Provenance Doctrine.

Latin as authorization. Open Crucible :33 calls Mu-jin's spoken Latin 'the authorization phrase'. Accord Latin :84 and :108 (no first person, so it cannot carry a warrant), Descent :57-58 and Summon Register :34 (Latin over the Parunic chain) put authorization in Parun. The Other wiki pages fix applies canon's side.
